ICJ

The Gambia v. Myanmar

Judgment on the merits
The Hague, 19 November 2026

Finding

Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya group in northern Rakhine State

During the 2017 “clearance operations”

Decided by 9 votes to 6

Myanmar also violated its duty to

Prevent genocideby individuals acting alongside its security forces
Punish genocideand other acts listed in the Convention
Enact legislationgiving effect to the Convention

The Court ordered Myanmar to

Investigate and, if warranted, prosecute suspects
Guarantee it will not happen again
Allow safe, voluntary and dignified return
Compensate the Rohingya for the damage caused

What happens next

2 years

for Myanmar to report on restitution and compensation

The judgment is final, without appeal, and binding on the parties.

Many voices. Many views.

Welcomedby some civil society and revolutionary groups
Worriedabout the impact on people already in hardship
Rejectedas unjust by some political groups

What we’ll discuss

1Perspectives and viewpoints following the ICJ ruling
2Potential situations and impacts arising from the ICJ ruling
3What needs to be considered and done to peacefully and constructively resolve this issue
